causesAndSolutions.cause: The control power voltage drops instantaneously.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the voltage drops during control power (L1C, L2C) cutoff or whether instantaneous power failure occurs. Measure whether the voltage input to the control circuit cable during operation is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 198 V to 264 V; 380 V servo drive: 342 V to 484 V
causesAndSolutions.solution: Restore system parameters to default values (2002-20h = 1), and write parameters again. Increase the power capacity or replace with a power supply of larger capacity.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Instantaneous power failure occurs during parameter saving.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether instantaneous power failure occurs during parameter saving.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Power on the system again, restore system parameters to default values (2002-20h = 1), and write parameters again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The number of write operations exceeds the limit.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether parameters are updated frequently through the host controller.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Change the write mode and write parameters again. If the servo drive is faulty, replace it.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The software has been updated.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the software has been updated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reset the servo drive model and the servo motor model, and restore system parameters to default values (2002-20h = 1).

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If the fault persists after several times of restart and parameter initialization, the servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Instantaneous power failure occurs during parameter saving.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether instantaneous power failure occurs during parameter saving.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the servo drive model (2001-0Bh) to a wrong value first and perform a power cycle, and then set the servo drive model to a correct value and perform a power cycle.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Instantaneous power failure occurs during the write operation.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether instantaneous power failure occurs during writing motor parameters.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Write motor parameters using the software tool.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The software has been updated.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the software has been updated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the servo drive model (2001-0Bh) to a wrong value first and perform a power cycle, and then set the servo drive model to a correct value and perform a power cycle.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If the fault persists after repeated execution of steps 1 and 2 and multiple times of restart, the servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA is faulty. The MCU cannot communicate with the FPGA.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Confirm whether the FPGA has been upgraded. Ensure the programming is successful. Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The software version of MCU or FPGA is wrong.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the MCU version (H01-00) is 9xx.x (the fourth digit displayed on the keypad is 9). Check whether the FPGA version (H01-01) is 9xx.x.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Contact Inovance for technical support and update to mutually-matching FPGA or MCU software.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The communication handshake between FPGA and HOST is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Access timeout occurs between HOST and the coprocessor.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The time interval of MCU torque interrupt scheduling is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The interrupt time of the current loop is too long.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the interrupt time of the torque loop is too long through the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Hide unnecessary functions.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An error occurs when writing parameters to EEPROM.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Modify a certain parameter value, power off and on the servo drive again, and check whether the modified value is saved.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the modified value is not saved and the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again, replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An error occurs when reading parameter values in EEPROM.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Modify a certain parameter value, power on the servo drive again, and check whether the modified value is saved.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the modified value is not saved and the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again, replace the servo drive.

subFaults.name: Invalid check on data written in EEPROM

causesAndSolutions.cause: The check on the data written in EEPROM fails.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Modify a certain parameter value, power off and on the servo drive again, and check whether the modified value is saved.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the modified value is not saved and the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again, replace the servo drive.

subFaults.name: Invalid check on data read in EEPROM

causesAndSolutions.cause: The check on the data read in EEPROM fails.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Modify a certain parameter value, power off and on the servo drive again, and check whether the modified value is saved.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the modified value is not saved and the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times, replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder model does not match the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the encoder model is correct.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the encoder.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor model is set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether H00-00 (Motor code) is set properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set H00-00 to a proper value that matches the motor model.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive model is set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether H01-10 (Servo drive series number) is set properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set H01-10 to a proper value that matches the servo drive model.

subFaults.name: Motor current and drive current mismatch

causesAndSolutions.cause: The internal scaling value is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the servo drive model is correct. If the rated current of the set servo drive model is larger than the rated current of the motor, calculation overflow will occur.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a servo drive of lower rated output current or a motor with higher rated current.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA does not support the motor encoder.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the motor encoder is supported by the FPGA version (H01-01).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Update FPGA software or replace the motor encoder.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor does not match the absolute position mode or the motor code is set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the motor nameplate to see whether the motor is equipped with an absolute encoder. Check whether 200D-01h (Motor code) is set properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 200D-01h (Motor code) correctly according to the motor nameplate or replace with a matching motor.

subFaults.name: Different DIs assigned with the same function

causesAndSolutions.cause: The same function is assigned to different DIs.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View 2003-03h, 2003-05h...2003-15h, 2017-01h, and 2017-03h...2017-1Fh to check whether they are assigned with the same DI function No.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Assign different DI functions to parameters that have been assigned with the same DI function. To enable such assignments, restart the control circuit or switch off the S-ON signal and send a 'RESET' signal.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The DI function No. exceeds maximum setting number allowed for DI functions.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the MCU software has been updated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Restore system parameters to default values (2002-20h = 1) and power off and on the servo drive again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The upper limit value of the mechanical single-turn position exceeds 2^31 in the absolute position rotation mode.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the mechanical gear ratio setpoint, the upper limit of the mechanical single-turn position and the electronic gear ratio in the absolute position rotation mode (H02-01 = 2).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reset the mechanical gear ratio, the upper limit of mechanical single-turn position and the electronic gear ratio to ensure the upper limit of the mechanical single-turn position (reference range) does not exceed 2^31.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive model does not match with the servo motor model.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View the servo drive and servo motor nameplates to check whether the devices used are Inovance SV660N series servo drive and servo motor.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with the mutually-matching servo drive and servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: A parameter check error occurs or no parameter is stored in the serial incremental encoder ROM.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the encoder cable provided by Inovance is used. Ensure the cable is intact and in good contact at both ends. Measure signals PS+, PS-, +5V and GND at both ends of the encoder cable and observe whether signals at both ends are consistent.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Use the encoder cable provided by Inovance. Ensure the cable is connected to the motor securely and tighten the screws on the servo drive side. Do not bundle encoder cables together with power cables (RST, UVW).

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: A fault occurs on the communication between FPGA and the motor encoder during initialization upon power-on.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Observe the value of H0B-28 to see whether it is not 0. Check whether the encoder cable is connected properly. Check whether the motor model is set properly. Check whether H01-00 (MCU software version) and H01-01 (FPGA software version) are correct.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the encoder cable, set the correct motor model, and ensure correct software versions are used.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encryption software is not programmed.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Power off and on again to check whether the fault persists.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Contact Inovance to program the encryption software again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The key of the encryption chip is incorrect, causing failure in decrypting the Renesas chip.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the software version. Check whether the encryption program is programmed in the servo drive. Check whether the encryption chip is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Power off and on the servo drive again, if the fault persists, contact Inovance for maintenance.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO is activated.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the STO function is activated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: There is no need to take any actions. Clear the fault through the fault reset function after the STO terminal is restored.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO power supply is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the 24 V power supply of the STO works normally. Measure the 24 V power supply of the STO to check whether it is stable.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Tighten the cables that are loose or disconnected.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO is inactive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after preceding actions are taken.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO power supply is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the 24 V power supply of the STO works normally. Measure the 24 V power supply of the STO to check whether it is stable.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Tighten the cables that are loose or disconnected.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO input resistor is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: After STO is triggered, only one STO signal is sent to MCU after the 24 V power supply is cut off due to input resistor drift.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The STO is inactive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after preceding actions are taken.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The 5 V power supply provided to the Buffer is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the 5 V power supply.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Short circuit occurs on the upstream optocoupler of STO1 or STO2.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The servo drive does not display E150.0 when the 24 V power supply is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The Buffer fails to block the PWM signals.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Gains are set improperly, leading to motor oscillation.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether vibration or sharp noise occurs during start and operation of the motor, or view the 'Current feedback' in the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder is wired improperly, aging, or connected loosely.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether encoder cables provided by Inovance are used. Check whether the encoder cable is aging, corroded, or connected loosely. Switch off the S-ON signal and rotate the motor shaft manually, observing whether the value of 200B-12h changes when the shaft rotates.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-solder, tighten or replace encoder cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cable but the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Overcurrent occurs on the regenerative resistor.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the resistance of the external regenerative resistor is too small or the regenerative resistor is short-circuited (between terminals P and C).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Select the resistance and model of the regenerative resistor again. Perform wiring again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are in poor contact.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether both ends of servo drive power cables and motor cables on servo drive UVW sides are loose and fall off.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Tighten the cables that are loose or fall off.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are grounded.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: After confirming the servo drive power cables and motor cables are connected properly, measure whether the insulation resistance between the servo drive UVW ends and the PE cable is at MΩ level.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor in case of poor insulation.

causesAndSolutions.cause: UVW cables of the motor are short-circuited.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and check whether short circuit occurs among UVW cables and whether burrs exist in the wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect the motor cables properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is damaged due to over-temperature.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and measure whether the resistance among UVW cables of the motor are balanced.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor if the resistance among UVW cables of the motor is unbalanced.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are in poor contact.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether both ends of servo drive power cables and motor cables on servo drive UVW sides are loose and fall off.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Tighten the cables that are loose or fall off.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are grounded.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: After confirming the servo drive power cables and motor cables are connected properly, measure whether the insulation resistance between the servo drive UVW ends and the PE cable is at MΩ level.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor in case of poor insulation.

causesAndSolutions.cause: UVW cables of the motor are short-circuited.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and check whether short circuit occurs among UVW cables and whether burrs exist in the wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect the motor cables properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is damaged due to over-temperature.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and measure whether the resistance among UVW cables of the motor are balanced.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor if the resistance among UVW cables of the motor is unbalanced.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are in poor contact.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether both ends of servo drive power cables and motor cables on servo drive UVW sides are loose and fall off.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Tighten the cables that are loose or fall off.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Motor cables are grounded.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: After confirming the servo drive power cables and motor cables are connected properly, measure whether the insulation resistance between the servo drive UVW ends and the PE cable is at MΩ level.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor in case of poor insulation.

causesAndSolutions.cause: UVW cables of the motor are short-circuited.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and check whether short circuit occurs among UVW cables and whether burrs exist in the wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect the motor cables properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is damaged due to over-temperature.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug the motor cables and measure whether the resistance among UVW cables of the motor are balanced.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the motor if the resistance among UVW cables of the motor is unbalanced. Perform wiring again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: MCU communication times out. (200B-2Eh = 1208)
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The internal integrated circuit is damaged.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: FPGA operation times out. (200B-2Eh = 0208)
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Figure out the cause according to cause 1.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive fails to receive the data fed back by the encoder in three consecutive cycles.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check bit12 of H0B-30. Check if encoder cable is connected properly, loose, too long, or suffering from interference. Check if motor model is correct. Check if encoder version (H00-04) is set properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect or replace the encoder cable. If servo drive operates improperly, replace it.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Phase-U and phase-V current samplings are abnormal. The internal current sampling integrated circuit is damaged.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether there is large equipment generating interferences on site and whether there are multiple interference sources in the cabinet.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the servo drive and motor are grounded and shielded properly. Install magnetic ring on the motor power cables and encoder cables. Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA operation times out. (200B-2Eh = 4208)
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The current loop operation times out.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Turn off some unnecessary functions to reduce the operating time of the current loop.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Power cables (UVW) of the servo drive are short-circuited to ground.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Unplug motor cables and check whether the servo drive power cables (UVW) are short circuited to ground (PE).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect or replace the servo drive power cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is short-circuited to ground.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: After confirming servo drive power cables and motor cables are connected securely, check whether the insulation resistance between servo drive UVW terminals and the grounding cable (PE) is at MΩ-level.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Disconnect servo drive power cables from the servo drive. The fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The UVW cables are connected in the wrong phase sequence.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether UVW phase sequence on the servo drive side is consistent with that on the motor side.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect UVW cables according to the correct phase sequence.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An error occurs on the initial phase detection of the motor rotor due to interference signals upon power-on.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The UVW phase sequence is correct, but E234.0 occurs when the servo drive is enabled.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Power off and on the servo drive again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder model is wrong or the wiring is incorrect.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the servo drive and servo motor nameplates to check whether the devices used are Inovance SV660N series servo drive and servo motor.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with the mutually-matching servo drive and servo motor. Check the motor model, encoder model, and encoder cable connections again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder cable is connected improperly, corroded or loose.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the encoder cable provided by Inovance is used. Check whether the cable is aging, corroded or loose. Switch off the S-ON signal, rotate the motor shaft manually, and check whether the value of 200B-0Bh (Electrical angle) changes when the motor shaft rotates.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-solder, tighten or replace the encoder cable.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The gravity load is too heavy in vertical axis applications.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the vertical axis load is too heavy. Adjust brake parameters 2002-0Ah...2002-0Dh and check whether the fault can be cleared.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reduce the load of the vertical axis, improve the stiffness level or hide this fault without affecting the safety performance or normal use.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Improper parameter settings cause excessive vibration.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The stiffness level is too high, leading to excessive vibration.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set a proper stiffness level to avoid excessive vibration.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The voltage input to the main circuit is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the power input specifications of the servo drive and measure whether the voltage input to main circuit cables (RST) on the servo drive side is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 198 V to 264 V; 380 V servo drive: 342 V to 484 V
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace or adjust the power supply according to the specified ranges.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The power supply is unstable or affected by the lightning strike.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the power input to the servo drive is unstable, affected by lightning strike or is within the preceding range.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect a surge protection device and then switch on the control circuit and main circuit. If the fault persists, replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The regenerative resistor fails.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If an internal regenerative resistor is used (2002-1Ah = 0), check whether terminals P and D are jumpered. If yes, measure the resistance between terminals C and D. If an external regenerative resistor is used (2002-1Ah = 1, 2), measure the resistance between terminals P and C.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the resistance is '∞' (infinite), the regenerative resistor is disconnected internally. If an internal regenerative resistor is used, replace with an external regenerative resistor and remove the jumper between terminals P and D. If an external regenerative resistor is used, replace with a new one. Set 2002-1Bh and 2002-1Ch according to the specifications.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The resistance of the external regenerative resistor is too large, and energy absorption during braking is insufficient.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the resistance of the external regenerative resistor between terminals P and C, and compare the measured value with the recommended value.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect a new external regenerative resistor of the recommended resistance between terminals P and C. Set 2002-1Bh and 2002-1Ch according to the specifications.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is in abrupt acceleration/deceleration status and the maximum braking energy exceeds the energy absorption value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Confirm the acceleration/deceleration time during operation and measure whether the DC bus voltage between terminals P and N exceeds the fault threshold during deceleration.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Ensure the voltage input to the main circuit is within the specified range, and then increase the acceleration/deceleration time if allowed.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The bus voltage sampling value deviates greatly from the measured value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the bus voltage (200B-1Bh) detected is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 200B-1Bh > 420 V; 380 V servo drive: 200B-1Bh > 760 V. Measure whether the DC bus voltage detected between terminals P and N is close to the value displayed in 200B-1Bh.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Contact Inovance for technical support.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after main circuit is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The main circuit power supply is unstable or fails.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the power input specifications of the servo drive. Measure whether the voltage input to the main circuit cables is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 198 V to 264 V; 380V servo drive: 342 V to 484 V. All the three phases must be measured.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the power capacity.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Instantaneous power failure occurs.
Voltage drop occurs on the power supply during operation.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Monitor the input voltage of the servo drive to check whether the same power supply is used to power up other devices, resulting in insufficient power capacity and voltage drop.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Phase loss: A single-phase power supply is used for a three-phase servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether main circuit cables are connected properly and whether the phase loss fault detection (200A-01h) is hidden.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the cables and connect the main circuit cables properly. Three-phase: R, S, T

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the bus voltage (200B-1Bh) detected is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 200B-1Bh < 200 V (or < 180 V for 750 W servo drives); 380 V servo drive: 200B-1Bh < 380 V. The fault persists after the main circuit is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The three-phase input cables are connected improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether cables between the power supply side and main circuit input terminals (R/S/T) are in good condition and connected properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the cables and connect the main circuit cables properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: A single-phase power supply is applied to a three-phase servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the power input specifications of the servo drive and measure whether the voltage input to the main circuit is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 198 V to 264 V; 380 V servo drive: 342 V to 484 V. All the three phases must be measured.
causesAndSolutions.solution: A three-phase servo drive of 0.75 kW (2001-03h = 5) is allowed to run under a single-phase power supply. If the input voltage complies with the specifications, set 200A-01h to 2 (Power input phase loss warning and fault inhibited). If input voltage does not comply with the specifications, replace or adjust the power supply.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The three-phase power supply is unbalanced or the voltage of all the three phases is too low.
The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after the main circuit (L1, L2, L3) is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The power supply of the control circuit is unstable or the voltage of the power supply drops.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the fault occurs during control circuit power supply (L1C, L2C) cutoff or during instantaneous power failure. Measure whether the voltage input to the control circuit cable is within the following range: 220 V servo drive: 198 V to 264 V; 380 V servo drive: 342 V to 484 V
causesAndSolutions.solution: Restore system parameters to default values (2002-20h = 1), and write parameters again. Increase the power capacity.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The control circuit cables are in poor contact
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether control circuit cables are connected properly and measure whether the voltage of the control circuit cable on the servo drive side is within the preceding range.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect or replace the cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The UVW phase sequence of motor cables is incorrect.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether UVW phase sequence on the servo drive side is consistent with that on the motor side.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect UVW cables according to the correct phase sequence.

causesAndSolutions.cause: 200A-09h is set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the overspeed threshold is lower than the maximum motor speed required in actual applications. Overspeed threshold = 1.2 x Maximum motor speed (200A-09h = 0); Overspeed threshold = 200A-09h (the setpoint of 200A-09h is not 0 and less than 1.2 times the maximum motor speed).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reset the overspeed threshold according to actual mechanical requirements.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The input reference is higher than the overspeed threshold.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the motor speed corresponding to the input reference exceeds the overspeed threshold. Refer to the manual for details on each control mode.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Position control mode: In CSP mode, decrease the position reference increment per synchronization cycle. In PP mode, decrease the value of 6081h or increase the acceleration and deceleration ramps. HM: Decrease the values of 6099-01h and 6099-02h, or increase the acceleration/deceleration ramp. Reduce the gear ratio. Speed mode: Decrease the target velocity, speed limit, and gear ratio. In PV mode, increase the speed ramps. Torque control mode: Set the speed limit to a value lower than the overspeed threshold.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor speed overshoots.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the speed feedback exceeds the overspeed threshold using the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains or operating conditions of the machine.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA speed measurement is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether bit9 of H0B-30 is 1.
causesAndSolutions.solution: The speed feedback is abnormal, check whether the encoder version (H00-04) is proper. Replace the encoder cables. The encoder cables suffer from interference. Re-connect the grounding cable and the shielded cable or install a magnetic ring on the encoder cable.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The MCU detects excessive pulse increment fed back by the FPGA.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of H0B-17 changes abruptly. Check whether the communication between the servo drive and the encoder suffers from interference.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Modify the value of H0A-70 (Overspeed threshold).

causesAndSolutions.cause: An encoder feedback error occurs.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the encoder communication suffers from interference.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the wiring of the encoder.

subFaults.name: Wrong UVW phase sequence detected during angle auto-tuning

causesAndSolutions.cause: The UVW cables are connected reversely, which is detected during angle auto-tuning.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Exchange the cables of any two phases of UVW and perform auto-tuning again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Speeds of servo drives in sizes A and B exceed the rated speed upon servo ON.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the motor is in the power generating state.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reduce the speed and switch on the S-ON signal again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor and encoder cable is connected improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the wiring among the servo drive, servo motor and encoder according to the correct wiring diagram.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect cables according to the correct wiring diagram. It is recommended to use the cables provided by Inovance.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The load is too heavy. The motor keeps outputting an effective torque higher than the rated value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the overload characteristics of the servo drive or servo motor. Check whether the average load ratio (200B-0DH) keeps exceeding 100.0%.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a servo drive of large capacity and a matching servo motor, or reduce the load and increase the acceleration/deceleration time.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Acceleration/Deceleration is too frequent or the load inertia is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Calculate the mechanical inertia ratio or perform inertia auto-tuning, and view the value of 2008-10h (Load inertia ratio). Confirm the individual operation cycle for cyclic operation.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the acceleration/deceleration time of an individual operation cycle.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Gains are improper or the stiffness level is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Observe whether the motor vibrates and generates abnormal noise during operation.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive or motor models are set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the motor model in 2000-06h and servo drive model in 2001-0Bh.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Read the servo drive nameplate and set the servo drive model and motor model properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is stalled due to mechanical factors, resulting in overload during operation.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the reference and motor speed (200B-01h) through the software tool or the keypad.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Eliminate mechanical factors.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault persists after servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Power output phase (UVW) loss or incorrect phase sequence occurs on the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Perform motor trial run without load and check cable connections and the phase sequence.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the cables according to the correct wiring diagram or replace the cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor parameters (especially the pole pairs) are set improperly and motor angle auto-tuning is not performed.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Read parameters in group H00 to check whether the pole pairs are set properly. Perform angle auto-tuning on the motor several times and check whether the value of H00-28 remains unchanged.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Modify motor parameter values.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The communication commands suffer from interference.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether jitter occurs on the commands sent from the host controller and whether EtherCAT communication suffers from interference.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the communication circuit between the host controller and the servo drive suffers from interference.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is stalled due to mechanical factors.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the reference and motor speed (H0B-00) through the software tool or the keypad.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether any mechanical part gets stuck or eccentric.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The ambient temperature is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the ambient temperature.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Improve cooling conditions to lower down the ambient temperature.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is powered off frequently to reset the overload fault.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View the fault log to see whether an overload fault or warning is reported.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Change the fault reset mode and perform reset 30s after overload. Increase the capacities of the servo drive and servo motor. Increase the acceleration/deceleration time and reduce the load.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The fan is damaged.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the fan rotates during operation.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The installation direction and clearance of the servo drive are improper.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the servo drive is installed properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Install the servo drive according to the installation requirements.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The servo drive is restarted 5 min after power-off, but the fault persists.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Improve cooling conditions to lower down the ambient temperature.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Change the fault reset mode and perform reset 30s after overload. Increase the capacities of the servo drive and servo motor. Increase the acceleration/deceleration time and reduce the load.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Improve cooling conditions to lower down the ambient temperature.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is powered off frequently to reset the overload fault.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View the fault records.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Change the fault reset mode and perform reset 30s after overload. Increase the capacity of the servo drive and servo motor. Increase the acceleration/deceleration time and reduce the load.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The installation direction and clearance of the servo drive are improper.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the servo drive is installed properly.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Install the servo drive according to the installation requirements.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The servo drive is restarted 5 min after power-off, but the fault persists.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The temperature of the air-cooled motor is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure whether the temperature of the air-cooled motor is too high.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Cool the motor down.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Gains obtained from STune or ETune are wrong. Vibration cannot be suppressed and the internal gains reach the lower limit.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the notch manually if vibration cannot be suppressed. Check whether the positioning threshold is too small. Increase the reference acceleration/deceleration time. Modify the electronic gear ratio to improve the reference resolution, or increase the reference filter time in the parameter configuration interface and check whether cyclic vibration occurs on the machine.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The battery is not connected during power-off.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the battery is connected during power-off.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 200D-15h to 1 to clear the fault.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The battery voltage of the encoder is too low.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the battery voltage.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a new battery of the matching voltage.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Set 200D-15h to 2 to clear the fault. E733.0 persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The number of forward revolutions exceeds 32767 or the number of reverse revolutions exceeds 32768.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of H0B-70 (Number of absolute encoder revolutions) is 32767 or 32768 when the servo drive works in the absolute position linear mode (H02-01 = 1).
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set H0D-20 (Absolute encoder reset selection) to 2 (Reset the encoder fault and multi-turn data) and power on the servo drive again. Perform homing if necessary.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The communication between the servo drive and the encoder is abnormal.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of H0B-28 (Absolute encoder fault information given by FPGA) is not 0.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether H00-00 (Motor code) is set properly. Check whether the encoder cable is connected properly. Check whether the servo drive and servo motor are grounded properly. You can install a magnetic ring on the encoder cable to reduce interference.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An internal fault occurs on the encoder.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether bit7 of H0B-28 is 1.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the encoder version (H00-04) is proper. Check whether the encoder cable is in proper condition. Replace the servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An error occurs during writing the position offset after angle auto-tuning.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the encoder cable shield and the grounding cable are connected properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An encoder communication error or encoder fault is detected after servo drive initialization is done upon power-on. E755.0 will be reported when a multi-turn Nikon encoder that carries no battery for a long time is powered on again.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the encoder is wired correctly. Check whether there is large equipment generating interferences on site and whether connectors are loose or cables are broken.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Ensure the encoder cable is connected properly. Take proper shielding measures if the interference source does exist.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The temperature of the absolute encoder is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the encoder or motor temperature.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Switch off the S-ON signal to cool the encoder down.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Over-temperature, overspeed, or EEPROM access error is detected in the encoder.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The fault is detected by the Nikon encoder, and the servo drive only displays the fault.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set H0D-21 to 1 to clear the fault.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Power output (UVW) phase loss or incorrect phase sequence occurs on the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Perform motor trial run without load and check the cable connections.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the cables according to the correct wiring diagram or replace the cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive UVW cables or the encoder cable is disconnected.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the cables. The UVW phase sequence on the servo drive side must be consistent with that on the motor side. Replace with new cables if necessary and ensure the cables are connected properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is stalled due to mechanical factors.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the reference and motor speed (200B-01h) through the software tool or the keypad.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Eliminate mechanical factors.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive gains are too low.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the position loop gain and speed loop gain of the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains manually or perform gain auto-tuning.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The position reference increment is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the gear ratio and profile settings in different modes.
causesAndSolutions.solution: In CSP mode, decrease the position reference increment per synchronization cycle. In PP mode, decrease the value of 6081h or increase the acceleration/deceleration ramp. In HM mode, decrease the values of 6099-01h and 6099-02h, or increase the acceleration/deceleration ramp. Decrease the gear ratio.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The value of 6065h (Following error window) is too small in relative to the operating condition.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of 6065h is too small.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the value of 6065h.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive or servo motor is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Monitor the operating curves through the oscilloscope function of the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the position reference is not 0 but the position feedback is always 0, replace the servo drive or the servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Power output (UVW) phase loss or incorrect phase sequence occurs on the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Perform motor trial running without load and check the cable connections.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the cables according to the correct wiring diagram or replace the cables.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive UVW cables or the encoder cable is disconnected.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Re-connect the cables. The UVW phase sequence on the servo drive side must be consistent with that on the motor side. Replace with new cables if necessary and ensure the cables are connected properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is stalled due to mechanical factors.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the reference and motor speed (200B-01h) through the software tool or the keypad.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Eliminate mechanical factors.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive gains are too low.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the position loop gain and speed loop gain of the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains manually or perform gain auto-tuning.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The position reference increment is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the gear ratio and profile settings.
causesAndSolutions.solution: In CSP mode, decrease the position reference increment per synchronization cycle. In PP mode, decrease the value of 6081h or increase the acceleration/deceleration ramp. In HM mode, decrease the values of 6099-01h and 6099-02h, or increase the acceleration/deceleration ramp. Decrease the gear ratio.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The value of 6065h (Following error window) is too small in relative to the operating condition.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of 6065h is too small.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the value of 6065h.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive or the servo motor is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Monitor the operating curves through the oscilloscope function of the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the position reference is not 0 but the position feedback is always 0, replace the servo drive or the servo motor.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The serial incremental encoder cable is disconnected or loose.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the encoder cable connection.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check for wrong connection, disconnection and poor contact of the encoder cable. Route the motor cable and encoder cable through different routes.

causesAndSolutions.cause: An error occurs when reading/writing the RS485 encoder parameters.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If the fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times, the encoder is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo motor.

subFaults.name: Position reference increment too large for once

causesAndSolutions.cause: The target position increment is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the variation value between two adjacent target positions using the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the maximum motor speed fulfills the application requirements. If yes, reduce the target position reference increment. Before switching the mode or enabling the servo drive, check whether the target position is aligned with current position feedback. The communication time sequence of the host controller is abnormal, leading to slave data reception error. Check the communication time sequence of the host controller.

subFaults.name: Position reference increment too large continuously

causesAndSolutions.cause: The target position increment is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the variation value between two adjacent target positions by using the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the maximum motor speed fulfills the application requirements. If yes, reduce the target position reference increment. Before switching the mode or enabling the servo drive, check whether the target position is aligned with current position feedback. The communication time sequence of the host controller is abnormal, leading to slave data reception error. Check the communication time sequence of the host controller.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The target position is still in the process of transmission when the servo limit or software limit signal is activated and the 32-bit upper/low limit is reached.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the host controller continues sending commands after the overtravel warning occurs.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the servo limit signal (bit0 and bit1 of 60FD recommended) through the host controller. Stop sending limit direction references when the servo limit signal is detected to be active by the host controller.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The target position exceeds the upper/lower limit of the position in the single-turn absolute mode.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the target position setpoint is within the single-turn upper/lower limit.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the target position to a value within the upper/lower limit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The SYNC signal is not generated due to hardware errors.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the SYNC signal cycle is 0 through the oscilloscope in the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive. Contact Inovance for maintenance.

causesAndSolutions.cause: This fault is caused by mal-operation of the master or the operator.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the master switches the network status when the servo drive is enabled.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the network status switchover program of the host controller.

causesAndSolutions.cause: For servo drives with H01-00 (MCU software version) = 902.0 or earlier, the fault causes include all the causes for EE08.0, EE08.01, and EE08.3...EE08.6, without differentiation. For later versions, fault causes are further differentiated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: For drives with version 902.0 or earlier, check causes related to SYNC signal loss, network status switchover, LAN cable connection, data frame loss, transfer error, and update timeout.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The physical connection of the data link is unstable or the process data is lost due to plug-in/plug-out of the LAN cable.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the LAN cable of the servo drive is connected securely, whether violent vibration occurs on site, whether the LAN cable is plugged in or out, and whether the LAN cable provided by Inovance is used.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the connection condition of the network port through the value change of H0E-29 and replace with a new LAN cable.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The data is lost due to EMC interference, poor quality of the LAN cable or poor connection.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the high 16 bits of H0E-25 have values that are increasing.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the servo drive is grounded properly and rectify the EMC interference. Check whether the LAN cable used is the one designated by Inovance. Check whether the LAN cable is connected properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The upstream station detects that the data frame has been corrupted and marked, which is then transferred to the slave, leading to a warning report.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether a process unit error occurs due to transfer error (H0E-27) or invalid frame (H0E-28) upon occurrence of the fault and check whether no counting is performed in RX-ERR of Port0.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the upstream station to locate the fault cause.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The slave is in the OP status and does not receive the data frame in a long time.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check through the software tool whether the phase difference between SYNC and IRQ exceeds the value of H0E-22 multiplied by the communication cycle.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check whether the operation load of the master CPU is too large. Increase the communication time or set H0E-22 to a large value. Check whether link loss occurs on the upstream station.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The lower limit of the software is larger than or equal to the upper limit.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the values of 607D-01 and 607D-02.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reset the values of 607D-01 and 607D-02 and ensure the former is lower than the latter.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The home offset is beyond the software limit.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The home offset is beyond the software limit when the encoder works in the incremental mode, absolute linear mode, or single-turn absolute mode.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the home offset to a value within the software limit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The home offset is beyond the upper/lower limit in the rotation mode.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The home offset is beyond the mechanical single-turn upper/lower limit when the encoder works in the rotation mode.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the home offset to a value within the mechanical single-turn upper/low limit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The set electronic gear ratio exceeds the limit: (0.001, 4000 x Encoder resolution/10000).
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the ratio of 6091-01h to 6091-02h exceeds the preceding range.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the gear ratio to a value within the preceding range.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The communication synchronization clock is configured improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Replace with another master (such as Beckhoff or Omron PLCs) and perform tests to compare between different masters.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Rectify improper configurations.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The IN/OUT port of EtherCAT communication is connected reversely.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the IN/OUT port is connected reversely.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect the IN and OUT ports according to the correct sequence.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The slave controller integrated circuit is damaged.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If the problem persists after the master is replaced, measure the synchronization signal generated from the slave controller integrated circuit with an oscilloscope.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Contact Inovance for replacing the slave controller integrated circuit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The MCU pins are damaged.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Test the synchronization signal generated from the slave controller integrated circuit with an oscilloscope. If there is a signal, the pin of the MCU integrated circuit is damaged.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Contact Inovance for replacing the MCU integrated circuit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The number of the mapping objects in TPDO or RPDO exceeds 10.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the number of self-indexes configured in 1600h or 1A00h.
causesAndSolutions.solution: The number of the mapping objects in TPDO or RPDO cannot exceed 10.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The XML file is programmed in the EEPROM. The XML file in the EEPROM is modified unexpectedly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the XML version displayed in H0E-96 is normal.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Program the XML file.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The EtherCAT data in the EEPROM cannot be read.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: This fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The communication is normal but the message in the EEPROM is wrong or lost.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: This fault persists after the servo drive is powered off and on several times.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The FPGA firmware is not programmed.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of 2001-02h is 09xx.Y.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Program the FPGA firmware.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the faulty servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The synchronization cycle is not an integer multiple of 125 µs or 250 µs.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the setpoint of the synchronization cycle in the controller.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the value of synchronization cycle to an integer multiple of 125 µs or 250 µs.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Excessive number of synchronization cycle errors occur on the controller.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the synchronization cycle of the controller using a digital oscilloscope or the oscilloscope function in the software tool.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the value of 200E-21h.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Check that the module is installed properly and supplied with power.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the contact of the communication interface of the expansion module or restart the rack.

subFaults.name: The CH0 preset value is out of range.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The preset value is outside the allowed range.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the preset value within the required range. Check and correct the following settings: The single-ended counting function is enabled but the DI is not configured in counting mode. The single-ended interface enabled by the command is inconsistent with the counting interface configured for DI. The counter is configured as a differential interface, but DI0 and DI1 are both configured in counting mode. Check whether the signal type is within the allowed range. Allowed values: A/B phase single frequency, A/B phase 2x frequency, A/B phase 4x frequency, pulse + direction, CW/CCW, single-phase counting (A), single-phase counting (B). Ensure the minimum value of the CH0 counter is smaller than the maximum value. Ensure the unit pulse increment is not smaller than 1. Check whether the time base is within the allowed range. Check whether the filter parameter is within the allowed range. Check whether the frequency sampling time is within the allowed range. The reset function is enabled by the command, but the DI is not configured for the reset function. Configure the DI for the reset function. The preset function is enabled by the command, but the DI is not configured for the preset function. Configure the DI for the preset function.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is enabled internally at the same time when the S-ON signal is activated through communication.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the S-ON signal is sent from the host controller when auxiliary functions are used.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Switch off the S-ON signal sent from the host controller.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The S-ON signal is sent from the DI and the software tool simultaneously.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the S-ON signal is sent from the DI terminal and the software tool simultaneously.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Switch off the redundant S-ON signal.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The vibration cannot be suppressed.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Enable vibration suppression manually (H09-12 to H09-23) to eliminate the vibration.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The auto-tuned values fluctuate dramatically.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the maximum operating speed and reduce the acceleration/deceleration time during ETune operation. For screw mechanisms, shorten the stroke.

causesAndSolutions.cause: Mechanical connections of the load are loose or eccentric.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Rectify the mechanical fault.

causesAndSolutions.cause: A warning occurs during auto-tuning and causes interruption.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Clear the fault and perform inertia auto-tuning again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The vibration cannot be suppressed if the load carries large inertia.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the acceleration/deceleration time to ensure the motor current is not saturated.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The home switch fails.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: If the home switch is used, check whether FunIN.31 is assigned and check wiring. Manually change DI logic and observe 200B-04h. If Z signal is used, check DI functions (FunIN.14, FunIN.15, FunIN.31) and wiring.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Perform the homing operation correctly after fixing wiring or logic issues.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The set homing duration is too short.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the value of 2005-24h (Homing time limit) is too small.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the value of 2005-24h.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The speed in high-speed searching for the home switch signal is too low.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the distance between the initial position of homing and the home switch. Check whether the value of 6099-01h is too small.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the value of 6099-01h.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The home switch is set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the limit signals at both sides are activated simultaneously. Check whether the limit signal and the deceleration point signal/home signal are both activated.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the position of the hardware switch properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The homing method (0x6098) is set to a value outside the range of [-2 to 14] in the absolute position single-turn mode (H02-01 = 4).
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the setpoint of 0x6098.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 0x6098 to a value within the range.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The homing method (0x6098) is set to a value outside the ranges of [-2, 14], [17, 30], and [33,35] when the absolute position single-turn mode is not used.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the setpoint of 0x6098.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 0x6098 to a value within the range.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The encoder battery voltage is lower than 3.0 V.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the battery voltage.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a new battery of matching voltage.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The DI function 34 (FunIN.34: Emergency stop) is triggered.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the logic of the DI assigned with FunIN.34 is valid.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the operating mode and clear the DI signal without affecting the safety performance.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The function of either DI1 to DI5 is set to an invalid value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether 2003-03h, 2003-05h, 2003-07h...2003-09h, and 2003-0Bh are set to invalid values.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the DI function to a valid value.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The function of either DO1 to DO3 is set to an invalid value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether 2004-01h, 2004-03h, and 2004-05h are set to invalid values.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set the DO function to a valid value.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The model identification parameters are not written. The check bytes of model identification are incorrect.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: The warning persists after the servo drive is powered off and on again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Write the model identification parameters again. Set H01-72 to 1 to hide the model identification function.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor and encoder cables are connected improperly or in poor contact.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the wiring among the servo drive, servo motor and encoder according to the correct wiring diagram.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Connect cables based on the correct wiring diagram. It is recommended to use the cables provided by Inovance.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The load is too heavy. The motor keeps outputting an effective torque higher than the rated value.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the overload characteristics. Check whether the average load ratio (200B-0Dh) keeps exceeding 100.0%.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a servo drive of large capacity and a matching servo motor, or reduce the load and increase the acceleration/deceleration time.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The acceleration/deceleration is too frequent or the load inertia is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the mechanical inertia ratio or perform inertia auto-tuning. View the value of 2008-10h.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Increase the acceleration/deceleration time.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The gains are improper or the stiffness level is too high.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Observe whether the motor vibrates and generates abnormal noise during operation.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust the gains.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive or motor models are set improperly.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the motor model in 2000-06h and the servo drive model in 2001-0Bh.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Read the servo drive nameplate and set the servo drive model and motor model properly.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor is stalled due to mechanical factors, resulting in overload during operation.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the reference and motor speed (200B-01h) through the software tool or the keypad.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Rectify mechanical factors.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Power off and on the servo drive again.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the fault persists after restart, replace the servo drive.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The external regenerative resistor is connected improperly, disconnected or loose.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Remove the external regenerative resistor and measure whether the resistance is '∞' (infinite). Measure whether the resistance between terminals P and C is '∞'.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace with a new external regenerative resistor. Prepare a new cable and connect the external regenerative resistor between terminals P and C.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The cable between terminals P and D is shorted or disconnected when an internal regenerative resistor is used.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure whether the resistance between terminals P and D is '∞'.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Prepare a new cable to short terminals P and D.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The setting of 2002-1Ah is incorrect when an external regenerative resistor is used.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the setpoint of 2002-1Ah. Measure the resistance of the external regenerative resistor. Check whether the value of 2002-1Ch is larger than the actual resistance.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 2002-1Ah to a proper value: 1 (External, naturally ventilated) or 2 (External, forcible cooling).

causesAndSolutions.cause: The resistance of the external regenerative resistor used is too large.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Select a proper regenerative resistor according to Table 5-3 in the manual.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The value of 2002-1Ch (Resistance of external regenerative resistor) is larger than the resistance of the external regenerative resistor used.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Set 2002-1Ch according to the resistance of the external regenerative resistor used.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The voltage input to the main circuit exceeds the specified range.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the voltage input to the main circuit cable is within the specified range: 220 V: 198-264 V; 380 V: 342-484 V
causesAndSolutions.solution: Adjust or replace the power supply according to the specified range.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The load moment of inertia ratio is too large.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Perform inertia auto-tuning or calculate total mechanical inertia. Check if actual load inertia ratio exceeds 30.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Select an external regenerative resistor of large capacity and set 2002-1Bh accordingly. Select a servo drive of larger capacity. Reduce the load or increase acceleration/deceleration time if allowed.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The motor speed is too high, and deceleration is not done within the required time.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View the motor speed curve during cyclic motion and check whether the motor is in the deceleration status for a long time.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The capacity of the servo drive or regenerative resistor is insufficient.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: View the single-cycle speed curve of the motor and calculate whether the maximum braking energy can be absorbed completely.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive is faulty.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Replace the servo drive.

warnings.faultName: Resistance of external regenerative resistor too small

subFaults.name: Resistance of external regenerative resistor too small

causesAndSolutions.cause: When an external regenerative resistor is used (2002-1Ah = 1, 2), the resistance of the external regenerative resistor is smaller than the minimum value allowed by the servo drive.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Measure the resistance of the external regenerative resistor connected between terminals P and C and check whether it is smaller than the value of 2002-16h.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If yes, replace with an external regenerative resistor that matches the servo drive and set 2002-1Ch accordingly. If not, set 2002-1Ch according to the resistance of the external regenerative resistor used.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The estimated temperature of the braking transistor is higher than H0A-38 (Maximum protection threshold)
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check parameter H0A-38 setting and monitor braking transistor load.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Reduce braking load, increase deceleration time, or use external regenerative resistor with appropriate rating.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The parameters modified are those whose 'Effective time' is 'Next power-on'.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether modifications of these parameters can be effective at next power-on.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Power on the servo drive again.

causesAndSolutions.cause: A large number of parameters are modified and saved frequently to EEPROM (200E-02h = 1, 3).
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether parameters are modified quickly and frequently through the host controller.
causesAndSolutions.solution: For parameters that need not be saved in EEPROM, set 200E-02h to 0.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The logic of the DI assigned with FunIN.14 is valid (Forward driving inhibited).
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether a DI in group 2003h is assigned with FunIN.14 and check whether the DI logic of the corresponding bit of 200B-04h (Monitored DI status) is valid.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the operation mode and on the prerequisite of ensuring safety, send a reverse run command or rotate the motor to deactivate the logic of the DI assigned with FunIN.14.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive position feedback reaches the positive software position limit.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the position feedback (0x6064) is close to the value of 0x607D-02.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Ensure the travel distance of the load is within the software position limit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The logic of the DI assigned with FunIN.15 (Reverse driving inhibited) is valid.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether a DI in group 2003h is assigned with FunIN.15 and check whether the DI logic of the corresponding bit of 200B-04h (Monitored DI status) is valid.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the operation mode and on the prerequisite of ensuring safety, send a forward run command or rotate the motor to deactivate the logic of the DI assigned with FunIN.15.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The servo drive position feedback reaches the negative software position limit.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check whether the position feedback (0x6064) is close to the value of 0x607D-02.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Ensure the travel distance of the load is within the software position limit.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The attempt to write torque ripple compensation parameters to the encoder fails. An encoder data read/write error occurs.
causesAndSolutions.confirmingMethod: Check the wiring of the encoder.
causesAndSolutions.solution: If the fault persists after several attempts, contact Inovance for technical support.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The configuration parameters sent to the module are out of the specified range or do not meet the requirements.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Check the configuration parameters.

subFaults.name: The sending buffer of the RS485 module channel is full.

causesAndSolutions.cause: The data length sent from the module is too large, or the sending interval or baud rate is too low.
causesAndSolutions.solution: Decrease the length of data sent from the module, or increase the sending interval or baud rate.

subFaults.name: The receiving buffer of the RS485 module channel is full.

causesAndSolutions.solution: Decrease the length of data sent to the module or increase the sending interval.
